01. THE BILLY BUTCHER (featured/lead? I said the lead feature is #01)
Lines:
There once was a butcher, Bill,
Who ground every sausage with skill.
When his mince went astray,
He simply would say,
"It's the market, my friend — or I'll kill!"
Note: "FILED: BUTCHERS. The mince was never found. The market, we are told, was a cat."

02. THE BAKER OF BREAM STREET
Old Bill the baker, up at three,
Kneaded, shaped, with great ceremony;
From dawn he'd bake and sell
Till the market's opening bell,
Then charge double for the wee.
Note: "FILED: BAKERS. 'The wee' are the small ones. The wee were not consulted."

03. THE BOATMAN OF BRACKEN BAY
Old Bill the boatman, on the tide,
Would row his passengers with pride;
When a wave did sway
His little gray skiff away,
He'd call out: "All steady — glide!"
Note: "FILED: BOATMEN. The skiff was returned the next week. The passengers declined."
Image: bill-boatman-tide

04. THE BUTLER
A butler named Bill, starched to shine,
Polished every spoon in a line.
When a guest once asked why
He bowed so deep and shy,
He replied, "Sir — I polish time."
Note: "FILED: BUTLERS. Time has since requested a second butler."

05. THE BOOKBINDER
Young Bill the bookbinder — thread and twine —
Bound each cover, neat, and fine;
He stitched, till one night,
By a library's light,
He woke, book-bound, spine by spine.
Note: "FILED: BINDERS. The novel in question: 'Wuthering Heights.' (All of it. Including the margins.)"

06. THE BROKER
The broker, a fidgety Bill,
Called every crash "an excellent fill";
He shouted "Buy! Buy!"
As the red candles fly,
Then retired early to the hill.
Note: "FILED: BROKERS. The hill has since been a private road. The toll is 40%."

07. THE BELLMAN
The bellman Bill, who rang the three,
Was heard as far as the sea;
He'd bellow "UP!" from the tower—
The whole town would lower
Its blankets and cry, "Make us free!"
Note: "FILED: BELLMEN. The town voted for 'up' at nine. Bill, regretfully, agreed."

08. THE BLACKSMITH
The blacksmith Bill, hammer in hand,
Kept a business plan grand:
Nails at the morn,
Chains by the lawn,
Horseshoes — by sundown, as planned.
Note: "FILED: BLACKSMITHS. The lawn was replaced by a chain. Neighbors report no regrets."
Image: bill-blacksmith-forge

09. THE BEEKEEPER
The beekeeper, a timid Bill,
Addressed the swarm with a skill:
"Excuse the intrusion —
I mean no confusion."
The bees gave him honey, still.
Note: "FILED: BEEKEEPERS. The swarm's reply, transcribed: 'Hm.'"
Image: bill-bees-hive

10. THE BOTANIST
The botanist, who ran the show,
Tutted at each vine that would grow.
"Up with the trellis!"
He'd bellow at his parsley;
The garden filed a complaint, you know.
Note: "FILED: BOTANISTS. The complaint was a tomato. It was not heard."

11. THE BRIDGE-BUILDER
The bridge-builder, up at noon,
Hummed a waltz in a minor tune;
When a stone would not hold,
He'd tap it: "There — now we're gold."
And the footbridge was done, before June.
Note: "FILED: BUILDERS. The river objects that it was never asked. The river is usually like that."

12. THE BREWER
The brewer Bill, whose barley grew
In his cellar, beside the brew;
He tapped it and poured —
And the whole town was in accord:
"That's the stoutest of any I knew."
Note: "FILED: BREWERS. The barley grew best on limericks. This is a known effect."

13. THE BIBLIOPHILE
The bibliophile, a Bill,
Whose shelves leaned but would not spill;
He stacked, and he stacked,
Till the flat's walls went black,
Then bought ten more — that's a thrill.
Note: "FILED: READER. The books, as a group, have asked for more room. They have not been given it."

14. THE BULLDOZER DRIVER
The bulldozer driver, Bill, by two,
Would level the hills and the view.
When he spotted a flower,
He'd halt, and give it a shower;
The flower sued — and won, you know.
Note: "FILED: HEAVY MACHINERY. The court ordered one daffodil per acre. Bill complied. The daffodils did not."

15. THE BUS CONDUCTOR
The bus conductor, a spare Bill,
Called each stop with a great thrill;
When the route hit a flood,
He said, "You may swim — I'll
Row to the next stop on the hill."
Note: "FILED: CONDUCTORS. The flood was, on inspection, a canal. Bill rows regardless."

16. THE GENTLE BURGLAR
The burglar Bill, at the break of day,
Knocked and said, "I must steal away —
Two spoons, and a candle."
The owner: "Take the handle,
The sugar. The cat will say."
Note: "FILED: THIEVES (AMATEUR). The cat voted no. Bill left the spoons and the tea."

17. THE CHESS MASTER
The chess master, Bill, by the dawn,
Moved his knight and his pawn;
When his rival, her best,
Tapped the queen and said, "Rest.
I resign — I'd rather yawn."
Note: "FILED: CHESS. The game lasted four moves. The yawn, in hindsight, was the true checkmate."

18. THE CLOCKMAKER
The clockmaker, whose life was a clock,
Told the time to the tock.
When the chime was late,
He'd climb up, in his coat,
And knock at the sky with a rock.
Note: "FILED: HOROLOGY. The sky, we are told, has since been on time."

19. THE ORCHESTRA CONDUCTOR
The orchestra's Bill, spare and tall,
Conducted with a very small
Bow; when a cello
Once ignored his mellow,
He turned, and conducted the hall.
Note: "FILED: MUSIC. The hall, according to witnesses, was 'a bit loud but honest.'"

20. THE CARTOGRAPHER
The cartographer, who'd draw the map
Of the world — but there was a gap:
His own lane was missing,
And the ink was still hissing.
He said, "That's the sea," and took a nap.
Note: "FILED: MAPS. Surveyors have since marked the lane. Bill has since re-marked the sea."

21. THE DIVER
The diver Bill, who ran the pool,
Was the calmest man of the school;
When a pupil went round and round,
He'd surface, with a pound
Of coins: "The fee — ma'am, stay cool."
Note: "FILED: POOLS. The pupil's parents paid by card. The coins remain unaccounted for."

22. THE DENTIST
The dentist Bill, with a steady will,
Polished, pried, and worked the drill;
He'd say, "Open wide —"
And the patient would hide
Behind gauze, and whisper: "I'll."
Note: "FILED: DENTISTS. The drill has never, to date, been shown to be the issue."

23. THE ECONOMIST (keyword)
The economist Bill, who'd chart the bill
Of the nation — steady, and still;
When a price rose, once,
He'd nod: "That's the course —
The market billing its fill."
Note: "FILED: ECONOMICS. The chart on the facing page is not to scale. The market is never to scale."

Bill and Jurgen, the odd pair,

And the bill, half and half, they'd declare.

I have set down this ledger — it's begun;
But if you know a Bill
Who is no Bill at all,

Let me write the JS scramble function:

function scramble(el){
 const final = el.dataset.text || el.textContent;
 el.dataset.text = final;
 const chars = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ§&*#—";
 let frame = 0;
 const total = 34;
 const tick = () => {
   frame++;
   const done = Math.floor((frame/total)*final.length);
   let out = final.slice(0, done);
   for(let i=done;i<final.length;i++){
     out += final[i]===" " ? " " : chars[Math.floor(Math.random()*chars.length)];
   }
   el.textContent = out;
   if(frame<total) requestAnimationFrame(tick); else el.textContent = final;
 };
 tick();
}

function typeVerse(container, lines){
 container.innerHTML="";
 let li=0;
 const nextLine = () => {
   if(li>=lines.length) return;
   const outer=document.createElement('span'); outer.className='vline';
   const inner=document.createElement('span'); inner.style.setProperty('--i',0);
   outer.appendChild(inner); container.appendChild(outer);
   // Force reveal:
   requestAnimationFrame(()=> inner.classList.add('shown'));
   const text = lines[li]; let ci=0;
   const t = setInterval(()=>{
     inner.textContent = text.slice(0, ++ci);
     if(ci>=text.length){clearInterval(t); li++; setTimeout(nextLine, 120);}
   }, 22);
 };
 nextLine();
}

02:
Old Bill the baker, up at three,
Kneaded, shaped, with great ceremony;
From dawn he'd bake and sell
Till the market's opening bell,
Then charge double for the wee.

03:
Old Bill the boatman, on the tide,
Would row his passengers with pride;
When a wave did sway
His little gray skiff away,
He'd call out: "All steady — glide!"

04:
A butler named Bill, starched to shine,
Polished every spoon in a line.
When a guest once asked why
He bowed so deep and shy,
He replied: "Sir — I polish time."

05:
Young Bill the bookbinder — thread and twine —
Bound each cover, neat, and fine;
He stitched, till one night,
By a library's light,
He woke, book-bound, spine by spine.

06:
The broker, a fidgety Bill,
Called every crash "an excellent fill";
He shouted: "Buy! Buy!"
As the red candles fly,
Then retired early to the hill.

07:
The bellman Bill, who rang the three,
Was heard as far as the sea;
He'd bellow "UP!" from the tower—
The whole town would lower
Its blankets, and cry: "Make us free!"

08:
The blacksmith Bill, hammer in hand,
Kept a business plan grand:
Nails at the morn,
Chains by the lawn,
Horseshoes — by sundown, as planned.

09:
The beekeeper, a timid Bill,
Addressed the swarm with a skill:
"Excuse the intrusion —
I mean no confusion."
The bees gave him honey, still.

10:
The botanist, who ran the show,
Tutted at each vine that would grow.
"Up with the trellis!"
He'd bellow at his parsley;
The garden filed a complaint, you know.

11:
The bridge-builder, up at noon,
Hummed a waltz in a minor tune;
When a stone would not hold,
He'd tap it: "There — now we're gold."
And the footbridge was done, before June.

12:
The brewer Bill, whose barley grew
In his cellar, beside the brew;
He tapped it and poured —
And the whole town was in accord:
"That's the stoutest of any I knew."

13:
The bibliophile, a Bill,
Whose shelves leaned but would not spill;
He stacked, and he stacked,
Till the flat's walls went black,
Then bought ten more — that's a thrill.

14:
The bulldozer driver, Bill, by two,
Would level the hills and the view.
When he spotted a flower,
He'd halt, and give it a shower;
The flower sued — and won, you know.

15:
The bus conductor, a spare Bill,
Called each stop with a great thrill;
When the route hit a flood,
He said: "You may swim — I'll
Row to the next stop on the hill."

16:
The burglar Bill, at the break of day,
Knocked and said: "I must steal away —
Two spoons, and a candle."
The owner: "Take the handle,
The sugar. The cat will say."

17:
The chess master, Bill, by the dawn,
Moved his knight and his pawn;
When his rival, her best,
Tapped the queen and said: "Rest.
I resign — I'd rather yawn."

18:
The clockmaker, whose life was a clock,
Told the time to the tock.
When the chime was late,
He'd climb up, in his coat,
And knock at the sky with a rock.

19:
The orchestra's Bill, spare and tall,
Conducted with a very small
Bow; when a cello
Once ignored his mellow,
He turned, and conducted the hall.

20:
The cartographer, who'd draw the map
Of the world — but there was a gap:
His own lane was missing,
And the ink was still hissing.
He said: "That's the sea," and took a nap.

21:
The diver Bill, who ran the pool,
Was the calmest man of the school;
When a pupil went round and round,
He'd surface, with a pound
Of coins: "The fee — ma'am, stay cool."

22:
The dentist Bill, with a steady will,
Polished, pried, and worked the drill;
He'd say: "Open wide —"
And the patient would hide
Behind gauze, and whisper: "I'll."

23:
The economist Bill, who'd chart the bill
Of the nation — steady, and still;
When a price rose, once,
He'd nod: "That's the course —
The market billing its fill."

24:
Bill and Jurgen, the odd pair,
Kept a bar, and argued, in the air;
But at closing time,
They'd clink glasses in a chime,
And the bill, half and half, they'd declare.

25:
Of the twenty-five Bills, one by one,
I have set down this ledger — it's begun;
But if you know a Bill
Who is no Bill at all,
This page, friend, is not yet done.

.draft-stamp{position:absolute;top:14px;right:14px;border:2px solid var(--red);color:var(--red);
  font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:9px;letter-spacing:.26em;padding:6px 10px;transform:rotate(7deg);text-transform:uppercase}
.draft-stamp.pulse{animation:stampPulse .5s ease}
@keyframes stampPulse{0%{transform:rotate(7deg) scale(1.7);opacity:0}60%{transform:rotate(7deg) scale(.94);opacity:1}100%{transform:rotate(7deg) scale(1)}}
.compose-out .verse{font-size:1.15rem;line-height:1.75}
.compose-out .marg{margin-top:22px}

/* ---------- colophon ---------- */
.colophon{margin:76px 0 42px;border-top:4px solid var(--ink);position:relative;padding-top:14px}
.colophon::before{content:"";position:absolute;top:3px;left:0;right:0;border-top:1px solid var(--ink)}
.col-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1.2fr 1fr 1fr;gap:30px;padding:22px 0 26px}
.col-title{font-family:'Fraunces',serif;font-weight:820;font-variation-settings:'WONK' 1;font-size:1.7rem}
.col-title span{color:var(--red)}
.col-lines{font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:10px;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-soft);line-height:2.1}
.col-lines b{color:var(--red);font-weight:400}
.col-bottom{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:14px;flex-wrap:wrap;border-top:1px dashed rgba(37,28,17,.4);
  padding-top:14px;font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:9.5px;letter-spacing:.16em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-soft)}
.col-bottom .halb{color:var(--red)}

/* ---------- responsive ---------- */
@media(max-width:900px){
  .lead{grid-template-columns:1fr}
  .lead-text{border-right:0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--ink)}
  .ledger-grid{grid-template-columns:1fr}
  .index-grid{grid-template-columns:1fr}
  .compose{grid-template-columns:1fr}
  .mast-deck{grid-template-columns:1fr}
  .deck-lead{grid-row:auto}
  .col-grid{grid-template-columns:1fr}
}

/* ---------- reduced motion ---------- */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){
  html{scroll-behavior:auto}
  *,*::before,*::after{animation-duration:.001s!important;animation-iteration-count:1!important;transition-duration:.001s!important}
  .js .card-wrap{opacity:1;transform:none}
  .js .verse .vline>span{transform:none;transition:none}
  .js .mask-in{transform:none;animation:none}
  .js .stamp{opacity:1;animation:none}
  .js .telegram{opacity:1;transform:none}
  .ticker-track{animation:none}
  .kb img,.chart .live{animation:none}
  .in .chart .line,.chart .line{transition:none;stroke-dashoffset:0}
  .collage img{transition:none}
}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="noise" aria-hidden="true"></div>
<aside class="side-rail" aria-hidden="true"><span>BILLS IN THIS EDITION</span><i>✦</i><span>TWENTY-FIVE</span><i>✦</i><span>NO TWO ALIKE</span></aside>

<div class="page">
<div class="wrap">

  <!-- ==================== MASTHEAD ==================== -->
  <header class="masthead">
    <div class="topbar">
      <span>Vol. XXV — The Full Bills</span>
      <span>Pub. nightly, at the Gilded Bucket</span>
      <span class="price">Price: one shilling, or a limerick of your own</span>
    </div>
    <h1 class="mast-title">
      <span class="mask"><span class="mask-in">THE</span></span>
      <span class="mask"><span class="mask-in title-bill">BILL</span></span>
      <span class="mask"><span class="mask-in">GAZETTE</span></span>
    </h1>
    <div class="mast-deck">
      <p class="deck-lead" data-scramble>An almanack of twenty-five limericks, each concerning a man of that name.</p>
      <p class="deck-sub">Being a faithful and complete record of the name <em>Bill</em>, in all his trades — with marginalia, a plate of engravings, an index of his own making, and a word from <em>Jurgen</em>.</p>
      <p class="deck-sub">The act of 1842 is quoted in full on the last page. It is short.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="mast-rule" aria-hidden="true"></div>
  </header>
</div>

  <!-- ==================== TICKER ==================== -->
  <div class="ticker" aria-hidden="true">
    <div class="ticker-track">
      <div class="ticker-set">
        <span><b>✦</b> BILLS WANTED IN EVERY TRADE</span>
        <span><b>✦</b> THE ECONOMIST IS BILLING HIS OWN PAPER</span>
        <span><b>✦</b> JURGEN HAS AGREED, FINALLY, TO SPLIT</span>
        <span><b>✦</b> TWENTY-FIVE LIMERICKS, NONE OF THEM ABOUT A BILLFOLD</span>
        <span><b>✦</b> ACT OF 1842: NO BILL IS THE SAME BILL AS ANOTHER</span>
        <span><b>✦</b> A BILL MAY ALSO BE A YOUNG SALMON</span>
      </div>
      <div class="ticker-set">
        <span><b>✦</b> BILLS WANTED IN EVERY TRADE</span>
        <span><b>✦</b> THE ECONOMIST IS BILLING HIS OWN PAPER</span>
        <span><b>✦</b> JURGEN HAS AGREED, FINALLY, TO SPLIT</span>
        <span><b>✦</b> TWENTY-FIVE LIMERICKS, NONE OF THEM ABOUT A BILLFOLD</span>
        <span><b>✦</b> ACT OF 1842: NO BILL IS THE SAME BILL AS ANOTHER</span>
        <span><b>✦</b> A BILL MAY ALSO BE A YOUNG SALMON</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>

<main class="wrap">

  <!-- ==================== THE LEAD BILL (No. 01) ==================== -->
  <section class="lead" id="no-01" data-io aria-labelledby="lead-name">
    <div class="lead-text">
      <p class="lead-kicker">No. 01 · Filed under: Butchers · Read first, by tradition</p>
      <h2 class="lead-name" id="lead-name">The Billy Butcher</h2>
      <div class="verse verse-lg">
        <span class="vline" style="--i:0"><span><span class="dc">T</span>here once was a butcher, Bill,</span></span>
        <span class="vline" style="--i:1"><span>Who ground every sausage with skill.</span></span>
        <span class="vline" style="--i:2"><span>When his mince went astray,</span></span>
        <span class="vline" style="--i:3"><span>He simply would say,</span></span>
        <span class="vline" style="--i:4"><span>“It’s the market, my friend — or I’ll kill!”</span></span>
      </div>
      <p class="marg"><span class="star">*</span> The mince was never found. The market, we are told, was a cat.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lead-art kb">
      <div class="stamp" aria-hidden="true"><span>The Lead<br>Bill<br>· est. 5 ·</span></div>
      <div class="frame"><img src="https://picsum.photos/seed/bill-butcher-bench/700/520" alt="An engraved study of the Billy Butcher at his bench" loading="eager"></div>
      <p class="lead-cap">Pl. i — The Billy Butcher, at his bench (study in sepia)</p>
    </div>
  </section>

  <!-- ==================== INDEX ==================== -->
  <section class="index-sec" aria-labelledby="idx-title">
    <div class="sec-head">
      <h2 class="sec-title" id="idx-title" data-scramble>Index of Bills</h2>
      <p class="sec-meta">A–Z by first initial, which is to say, alphabetically</p>
    </div>
    <div class="index-grid">
      <a class="idx" href="#no-01"><span class="idx-no">01</span><span class="idx-name">The Billy Butcher</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">2</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-02"><span class="idx-no">02</span><span class="idx-name">The Baker of Bream Street</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">3</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-03"><span class="idx-no">03</span><span class="idx-name">The Boatman of Bracken Bay</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">4</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-04"><span class="idx-no">04</span><span class="idx-name">The Butler</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">5</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-05"><span class="idx-no">05</span><span class="idx-name">The Bookbinder</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">6</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-06"><span class="idx-no">06</span><span class="idx-name">The Broker</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">7</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-07"><span class="idx-no">07</span><span class="idx-name">The Bellman</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">8</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-08"><span class="idx-no">08</span><span class="idx-name">The Blacksmith</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">9</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-09"><span class="idx-no">09</span><span class="idx-name">The Beekeeper</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">10</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-10"><span class="idx-no">10</span><span class="idx-name">The Botanist</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">11</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-11"><span class="idx-no">11</span><span class="idx-name">The Bridge-Builder</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">12</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-12"><span class="idx-no">12</span><span class="idx-name">The Brewer</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">13</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-13"><span class="idx-no">13</span><span class="idx-name">The Bibliophile</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">14</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-14"><span class="idx-no">14</span><span class="idx-name">The Bulldozer Driver</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">15</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-15"><span class="idx-no">15</span><span class="idx-name">The Bus Conductor</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">16</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-16"><span class="idx-no">16</span><span class="idx-name">The Gentle Burglar</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">17</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-17"><span class="idx-no">17</span><span class="idx-name">The Chess Master</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">18</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-18"><span class="idx-no">18</span><span class="idx-name">The Clockmaker</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">19</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-19"><span class="idx-no">19</span><span class="idx-name">The Orchestra Conductor</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">20</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-20"><span class="idx-no">20</span><span class="idx-name">The Cartographer</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">21</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-21"><span class="idx-no">21</span><span class="idx-name">The Diver</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">22</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-22"><span class="idx-no">22</span><span class="idx-name">The Dentist</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">23</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-23"><span class="idx-no">23</span><span class="idx-name">The Economist</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">24</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-24"><span class="idx-no">24</span><span class="idx-name">Bill and Jurgen</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">25</span></a>
      <a class="idx" href="#no-25"><span class="idx-no">25</span><span class="idx-name">The Last Bill</span><span class="idx-dots"></span><span class="idx-pg">26</span></a>
    </div>
  </section>

  <!-- ==================== THE LEDGER ==================== -->
  <section class="ledger" aria-labelledby="ledger-title">
    <div class="sec-head">
      <h2 class="sec-title" id="ledger-title" data-scramble>The Ledger</h2>
      <p class="sec-meta">Twenty-four entries — No. 01 leads above</p>
    </div>

    <div class="ledger-grid">

      <div class="card-wrap" data-io>
        <article class="bill-card" id="no-02">
          <div class="card-top"><span class="no">No. 02</span><span>Filed: Bakers</span></div>
          <h3 class="bill-name">The Baker of Bream Street</h3>
          <div class="verse">
            <span class="vline" style="--i:0"><span>Old Bill the baker, up at three,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:1"><span>Kneaded, shaped, with great ceremony;</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:2"><span>From dawn he’d bake and sell</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:3"><span>Till the market’s opening bell,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:4"><span>Then charge double for the wee.</span></span>
          </div>
          <p class="marg"><span class="star">*</span> The “wee” are the small ones. The wee were not consulted.</p>
          <div class="seal" aria-hidden="true">B</div>
        </article>
      </div>

      <div class="card-wrap" data-io>
        <article class="bill-card" id="no-03">
          <div class="card-top"><span class="no">No. 03</span><span>Filed: Boatmen</span></div>
          <h3 class="bill-name">The Boatman of Bracken Bay</h3>
          <div class="verse">
            <span class="vline" style="--i:0"><span>Old Bill the boatman, on the tide,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:1"><span>Would row his passengers with pride;</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:2"><span>When a wave did sway</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:3"><span>His little gray skiff away,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:4"><span>He’d call out: “All steady — glide!”</span></span>
          </div>
          <figure class="card-art kb">
            <div class="frame"><img src="https://picsum.photos/seed/bill-boatman-tide/620/330" alt="The boatman offshore at Bracken Bay, engraving" loading="lazy"></div>
            <figcaption>The subject, offshore (Bracken Bay)</figcaption>
          </figure>
          <p class="marg"><span class="star">*</span> The skiff was returned the next week. The passengers, regrettably, declined it.</p>
          <div class="seal" aria-hidden="true">B</div>
        </article>
      </div>

      <div class="card-wrap" data-io>
        <article class="bill-card" id="no-04">
          <div class="card-top"><span class="no">No. 04</span><span>Filed: Butlers</span></div>
          <h3 class="bill-name">The Butler</h3>
          <div class="verse">
            <span class="vline" style="--i:0"><span>A butler named Bill, starched to shine,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:1"><span>Polished every spoon in a line.</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:2"><span>When a guest once asked why</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:3"><span>He bowed so deep and shy,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:4"><span>He replied: “Sir — I polish time.”</span></span>
          </div>
          <p class="marg"><span class="star">*</span> Time has since asked for a second butler. The household refused.</p>
          <div class="seal" aria-hidden="true">B</div>
        </article>
      </div>

      <div class="card-wrap" data-io>
        <article class="bill-card" id="no-05">
          <div class="card-top"><span class="no">No. 05</span><span>Filed: Binders</span></div>
          <h3 class="bill-name">The Bookbinder</h3>
          <div class="verse">
            <span class="vline" style="--i:0"><span>Young Bill the bookbinder — thread and twine —</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:1"><span>Bound each cover, neat, and fine;</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:2"><span>He stitched, till one night,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:3"><span>By a library’s light,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:4"><span>He woke, book-bound, spine by spine.</span></span>
          </div>
          <p class="marg"><span class="star">*</span> The novel in question: <em>Wuthering Heights</em>. All of it, including the margins.</p>
          <div class="seal" aria-hidden="true">B</div>
        </article>
      </div>

      <div class="card-wrap" data-io>
        <article class="bill-card" id="no-06">
          <div class="card-top"><span class="no">No. 06</span><span>Filed: Brokers</span></div>
          <h3 class="bill-name">The Broker</h3>
          <div class="verse">
            <span class="vline" style="--i:0"><span>The broker, a fidgety Bill,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:1"><span>Called every crash “an excellent fill”;</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:2"><span>He shouted: “Buy! Buy!”</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:3"><span>As the red candles fly,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:4"><span>Then retired early to the hill.</span></span>
          </div>
          <p class="marg"><span class="star">*</span> The hill is now a private road. The toll is forty percent.</p>
          <div class="seal" aria-hidden="true">B</div>
        </article>
      </div>

      <div class="card-wrap" data-io>
        <article class="bill-card" id="no-07">
          <div class="card-top"><span class="no">No. 07</span><span>Filed: Bellmen</span></div>
          <h3 class="bill-name">The Bellman</h3>
          <div class="verse">
            <span class="vline" style="--i:0"><span>The bellman Bill, who rang the three,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:1"><span>Was heard as far as the sea;</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:2"><span>He’d bellow “UP!” from the tower—</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:3"><span>The whole town would lower</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:4"><span>Its blankets, and cry: “Make us free!”</span></span>
          </div>
          <p class="marg"><span class="star">*</span> The town voted for “up” at nine. Bill, after consultation, agreed.</p>
          <div class="seal" aria-hidden="true">B</div>
        </article>
      </div>

      <div class="card-wrap" data-io>
        <article class="bill-card" id="no-08">
          <div class="card-top"><span class="no">No. 08</span><span>Filed: Blacksmiths</span></div>
          <h3 class="bill-name">The Blacksmith</h3>
          <div class="verse">
            <span class="vline" style="--i:0"><span>The blacksmith Bill, hammer in hand,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:1"><span>Kept a business plan grand:</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:2"><span>Nails at the morn,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:3"><span>Chains by the lawn,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:4"><span>Horseshoes — by sundown, as planned.</span></span>
          </div>
          <figure class="card-art kb">
            <div class="frame"><img src="https://picsum.photos/seed/bill-blacksmith-forge/620/330" alt="A forge at dawn, engraving" loading="lazy"></div>
            <figcaption>The forge, lit at dawn</figcaption>
          </figure>
          <p class="marg"><span class="star">*</span> The lawn has been replaced by a chain. Neighbors report no regrets.</p>
          <div class="seal" aria-hidden="true">B</div>
        </article>
      </div>

      <div class="card-wrap" data-io>
        <article class="bill-card" id="no-09">
          <div class="card-top"><span class="no">No. 09</span><span>Filed: Beekeepers</span></div>
          <h3 class="bill-name">The Beekeeper</h3>
          <div class="verse">
            <span class="vline" style="--i:0"><span>The beekeeper, a timid Bill,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:1"><span>Addressed the swarm with a skill:</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:2"><span>“Excuse the intrusion —</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:3"><span>I mean no confusion.”</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:4"><span>The bees gave him honey, still.</span></span>
          </div>
          <figure class="card-art kb">
            <div class="frame"><img src="https://picsum.photos/seed/bill-bees-hive/620/330" alt="A hive in a hedgerow, engraving" loading="lazy"></div>
            <figcaption>The hive, addressed (No. 09)</figcaption>
          </figure>
          <p class="marg"><span class="star">*</span> The swarm’s reply, transcribed: “Hm.”</p>
          <div class="seal" aria-hidden="true">B</div>
        </article>
      </div>

      <div class="card-wrap" data-io>
        <article class="bill-card" id="no-10">
          <div class="card-top"><span class="no">No. 10</span><span>Filed: Botanists</span></div>
          <h3 class="bill-name">The Botanist</h3>
          <div class="verse">
            <span class="vline" style="--i:0"><span>The botanist, who ran the show,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:1"><span>Tutted at each vine that would grow.</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:2"><span>“Up with the trellis!”</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:3"><span>He’d bellow at his parsley;</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:4"><span>The garden filed a complaint, you know.</span></span>
          </div>
          <p class="marg"><span class="star">*</span> The complaint was a tomato. It has not been heard.</p>
          <div class="seal" aria-hidden="true">B</div>
        </article>
      </div>

      <div class="card-wrap" data-io>
        <article class="bill-card" id="no-11">
          <div class="card-top"><span class="no">No. 11</span><span>Filed: Bridges</span></div>
          <h3 class="bill-name">The Bridge-Builder</h3>
          <div class="verse">
            <span class="vline" style="--i:0"><span>The bridge-builder, up at noon,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:1"><span>Hummed a waltz in a minor tune;</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:2"><span>When a stone would not hold,</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:3"><span>He’d tap it: “There — now we’re gold.”</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:4"><span>And the footbridge was done, before June.</span></span>
          </div>
          <p class="marg"><span class="star">*</span> The river objects that it was never asked. The river is usually like that.</p>
          <div class="seal" aria-hidden="true">B</div>
        </article>
      </div>

      <div class="card-wrap" data-io>
        <article class="bill-card" id="no-12">
          <div class="card-top"><span class="no">No. 12</span><span>Filed: Brewers</span></div>
          <h3 class="bill-name">The Brewer</h3>
          <div class="verse">
            <span class="vline" style="--i:0"><span>The brewer Bill, whose barley grew</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:1"><span>In his cellar, beside the brew;</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:2"><span>He tapped it and poured —</span></span>
            <span class="vline" style="--i:3"><span>And the whole town was in accord:</span></span>

Note: "FILED: BEEKEEPERS. The swarm's reply, transcribed: 'Hm.'"
Image: bill-bees-hive

10. THE BOTANIST
The botanist, who ran the show,
Tutted at each vine that would grow.
"Up with the trellis!"
He'd bellow at his parsley;
The garden filed a complaint, you know.
Note: "FILED: BOTANISTS. The complaint was a tomato. It was not heard."

11. THE BRIDGE-BUILDER
The bridge-builder, up at noon,
Hummed a waltz in a minor tune;
When a stone would not hold,
He'd tap it: "There — now we're gold."
And the footbridge was done, before June.
Note: "FILED: BUILDERS. The river objects that it was never asked. The river is usually like that."

12. THE BREWER
The brewer Bill, whose barley grew
In his cellar, beside the brew;
He tapped it and poured —
And the whole town was in accord:
"That's the stoutest of any I knew."
Note: "FILED: BREWERS. The barley grew best on limericks. This is a known effect."

13. THE BIBLIOPHILE
The bibliophile, a Bill,
Whose shelves leaned but would not spill;
He stacked, and he stacked,
Till the flat's walls went black,
Then bought ten more — that's a thrill.
Note: "FILED: READER. The books, as a group, have asked for more room. They have not been given it."

14. THE BULLDOZER DRIVER
The bulldozer driver, Bill, by two,
Would level the hills and the view.
When he spotted a flower,
He'd halt, and give it a shower;
The flower sued — and won, you know.
Note: "FILED: HEAVY MACHINERY. The court ordered one daffodil per acre. Bill complied. The daffodils did not."

15. THE BUS CONDUCTOR
The bus conductor, a spare Bill,
Called each stop with a great thrill;
When the route hit a flood,
He said, "You may swim — I'll
Row to the next stop on the hill."
Note: "FILED: CONDUCTORS. The flood was, on inspection, a canal. Bill rows regardless."

16. THE GENTLE BURGLAR
The burglar Bill, at the break of day,
Knocked and said, "I must steal away —
Two spoons, and a candle."
The owner: "Take the handle,
The sugar. The cat will say."
Note: "FILED: THIEVES (AMATEUR). The cat voted no. Bill left the spoons and the tea."

17. THE CHESS MASTER
The chess master, Bill, by the dawn,
Moved his knight and his pawn;
When his rival, her best,
Tapped the queen and said, "Rest.
I resign — I'd rather yawn."
Note: "FILED: CHESS. The game lasted four moves. The yawn, in hindsight, was the true checkmate."

18. THE CLOCKMAKER
The clockmaker, whose life was a clock,
Told the time to the tock.
When the chime was late,
He'd climb up, in his coat,
And knock at the sky with a rock.
Note: "FILED: HOROLOGY. The sky, we are told, has since been on time."

19. THE ORCHESTRA CONDUCTOR
The orchestra's Bill, spare and tall,
Conducted with a very small
Bow; when a cello
Once ignored his mellow,
He turned, and conducted the hall.
Note: "FILED: MUSIC. The hall, according to witnesses, was 'a bit loud but honest.'"

20. THE CARTOGRAPHER
The cartographer, who'd draw the map
Of the world — but there was a gap:
His own lane was missing,
And the ink was still hissing.
He said, "That's the sea," and took a nap.
Note: "FILED: MAPS. Surveyors have since marked the lane. Bill has since re-marked the sea."

21. THE DIVER
The diver Bill, who ran the pool,
Was the calmest man of the school;
When a pupil went round and round,
He'd surface, with a pound
Of coins: "The fee — ma'am, stay cool."
Note: "FILED: POOLS. The pupil's parents paid by card. The coins remain unaccounted for."

22. THE DENTIST
The dentist Bill, with a steady will,
Polished, pried, and worked the drill;
He'd say, "Open wide —"
And the patient would hide
Behind gauze, and whisper: "I'll."
Note: "FILED: DENTISTS. The drill has never, to date, been shown to be the issue."

23. THE ECONOMIST (keyword)
The economist Bill, who'd chart the bill
Of the nation — steady, and still;
When a price rose, once,
He'd nod: "That's the course —
The market billing its fill."
Note: "FILED: ECONOMICS. The chart on the facing page is not to scale. The market is never to scale."
+ an inline SVG line chart "THE INDEX OF BILLS (1842–1999)" that draws in.

24. BILL AND JURGEN (keyword)
Bill and Jurgen, the odd pair,
Kept a bar, and argued, in the air;
But at closing time,
They'd clink glasses in a chime,
And the bill, half and half, they'd declare.
Note: "FILED: BAR. JURGEN'S OWN WORDS, BELOW."
+ the telegram band below.

25. THE LAST BILL
Of the twenty-five Bills, one by one,
I have set down this ledger — it's begun;
But if you know a Bill
Who is no Bill at all,
This page, friend, is not yet done.
Note: "FILED: EVERYTHING. A bill, here, may be a young salmon. The editor takes no responsibility."

function scramble(el){
 const final = el.dataset.text || el.textContent;
 el.dataset.text = final;
 const chars = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ§&*#—";
 let frame = 0;
 const total = 34;
 const tick = () => {
   frame++;
   const done = Math.floor((frame/total)*final.length);
   let out = final.slice(0, done);
   for(let i=done;i<final.length;i++){
     out += final[i]===" " ? " " : chars[Math.floor(Math.random()*chars.length)];
   }
   el.textContent = out;
   if(frame<total) requestAnimationFrame(tick); else el.textContent = final;
 };
 tick();
}

function typeVerse(container, lines){
 container.innerHTML="";
 let li=0;
 const nextLine = () => {
   if(li>=lines.length) return;
   const outer=document.createElement('span'); outer.className='vline';
   const inner=document.createElement('span'); inner.style.setProperty('--i',0);
   outer.appendChild(inner); container.appendChild(outer);
   // Force reveal:
   requestAnimationFrame(()=> inner.classList.add('shown'));
   const text = lines[li]; let ci=0;
   const t = setInterval(()=>{
     inner.textContent = text.slice(0, ++ci);
     if(ci>=text.length){clearInterval(t); li++; setTimeout(nextLine, 120);}
   }, 22);
 };
 nextLine();
}

02:
Old Bill the baker, up at three,
Kneaded, shaped, with great ceremony;
From dawn he'd bake and sell
Till the market's opening bell,
Then charge double for the wee.

03:
Old Bill the boatman, on the tide,
Would row his passengers with pride;
When a wave did sway
His little gray skiff away,
He'd call out: "All steady — glide!"

04:
A butler named Bill, starched to shine,
Polished every spoon in a line.
When a guest once asked why
He bowed so deep and shy,
He replied: "Sir — I polish time."

05:
Young Bill the bookbinder — thread and twine —
Bound each cover, neat, and fine;
He stitched, till one night,
By a library's light,
He woke, book-bound, spine by spine.

06:
The broker, a fidgety Bill,
Called every crash "an excellent fill";
He shouted: "Buy! Buy!"
As the red candles fly,
Then retired early to the hill.

07:
The bellman Bill, who rang the three,
Was heard as far as the sea;
He'd bellow "UP!" from the tower—
The whole town would lower
Its blankets, and cry: "Make us free!"

08:
The blacksmith Bill, hammer in hand,
Kept a business plan grand:
Nails at the morn,
Chains by the lawn,
Horseshoes — by sundown, as planned.

09:
The beekeeper, a timid Bill,
Addressed the swarm with a skill:
"Excuse the intrusion —
I mean no confusion."
The bees gave him honey, still.

10:
The botanist, who ran the show,
Tutted at each vine that would grow.
"Up with the trellis!"
He'd bellow at his parsley;
The garden filed a complaint, you know.

11:
The bridge-builder, up at noon,
Hummed a waltz in a minor tune;
When a stone would not hold,
He'd tap it: "There — now we're gold."
And the footbridge was done, before June.

12:
The brewer Bill, whose barley grew
In his cellar, beside the brew;
He tapped it and poured —
And the whole town was in accord:
"That's the stoutest of any I knew."

13:
The bibliophile, a Bill,
Whose shelves leaned but would not spill;
He stacked, and he stacked,
Till the flat's walls went black,
Then bought ten more — that's a thrill.

14:
The bulldozer driver, Bill, by two,
Would level the hills and the view.
When he spotted a flower,
He'd halt, and give it a shower;
The flower sued — and won, you know.

15:
The bus conductor, a spare Bill,
Called each stop with a great thrill;
When the route hit a flood,
He said: "You may swim — I'll
Row to the next stop on the hill."

16:
The burglar Bill, at the break of day,
Knocked and said: "I must steal away —
Two spoons, and a candle."
The owner: "Take the handle,
The sugar. The cat will say."

17:
The chess master, Bill, by the dawn,
Moved his knight and his pawn;
When his rival, her best,
Tapped the queen and said: "Rest.
I resign — I'd rather yawn."

18:
The clockmaker, whose life was a clock,
Told the time to the tock.
When the chime was late,
He'd climb up, in his coat,
And knock at the sky with a rock.

19:
The orchestra's Bill, spare and tall,
Conducted with a very small
Bow; when a cello
Once ignored his mellow,
He turned, and conducted the hall.

20:
The cartographer, who'd draw the map
Of the world — but there was a gap:
His own lane was missing,
And the ink was still hissing.
He said: "That's the sea," and took a nap.

21:
The diver Bill, who ran the pool,
Was the calmest man of the school;
When a pupil went round and round,
He'd surface, with a pound
Of coins: "The fee — ma'am, stay cool."

22:
The dentist Bill, with a steady will,
Polished, pried, and worked the drill;
He'd say: "Open wide —"
And the patient would hide
Behind gauze, and whisper: "I'll."

23:
The economist Bill, who'd chart the bill
Of the nation — steady, and still;
When a price rose, once,
He'd nod: "That's the course —
The market billing its fill."

24:
Bill and Jurgen, the odd pair,
Kept a bar, and argued, in the air;
But at closing time,
They'd clink glasses in a chime,
And the bill, half and half, they'd declare.

25:
Of the twenty-five Bills, one by one,
I have set down this ledger — it's begun;
But if you know a Bill
Who is no Bill at all,
This page, friend, is not yet done.

.ticker-track{display:flex;width:max-content;animation:tick 46s linear infinite}
.ticker:hover .ticker-track{animation-play-state:paused}
.ticker-set{display:flex;white-space:nowrap;font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:11px;
  letter-spacing:.14em;text-transform:uppercase}
.ticker-set span{padding-right:2.6em}
.ticker-set b{color:var(--red-light);font-weight:400}
@keyframes tick{to{transform:translateX(-50%)}}

/* ---------- lead bill ---------- */
.lead{margin-top:38px;border:1px solid var(--ink);background:var(--card);
  box-shadow:9px 10px 0 rgba(37,28,17,.10);display:grid;grid-template-columns:1.08fr .92fr}
.lead-text{padding:30px clamp(22px,3vw,34px) 26px;border-right:1px solid var(--ink);position:relative}
.lead-kicker{font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:10.5px;letter-spacing:.2em;color:var(--red);text-transform:uppercase}
.lead-name{font-family:'Fraunces',Georgia,serif;font-weight:750;font-variation-settings:'WONK' 1;
  font-size:clamp(1.9rem,4vw,2.7rem);margin:10px 0 18px;letter-spacing:-.01em}
.verse{font-style:italic;font-weight:500;color:var(--ink)}
.verse .vline{display:block;overflow:hidden}
.verse .vline>span{display:inline-block}
.js .verse .vline>span{transform:translateY(112%);transition:transform .6s cubic-bezier(.2,.65,.25,1) calc(120ms + var(--i,0)*75ms)}
.js .in .verse .vline>span, .js .verse.in .vline>span{transform:translateY(0)}
.verse-lg{font-size:clamp(1.3rem,2.4vw,1.85rem);line-height:1.52}
.dc{font-family:'Fraunces',Georgia,serif;font-style:normal;font-weight:800;color:var(--red);
  font-size:3.1em;line-height:.8;float:left;margin:.06em .14em 0 0}
.marg{font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:10.5px;letter-spacing:.05em;text-transform:uppercase;
  color:var(--ink-soft);margin-top:18px;padding-top:11px;border-top:1px dashed rgba(37,28,17,.4);line-height:1.8}
.marg .star{color:var(--red)}
.lead-art{padding:26px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;position:relative}
.lead-art .frame{border:1px solid var(--ink);overflow:hidden}
.lead-art img{width:100%;display:block;filter:grayscale(.85) sepia(.38) contrast(1.02)}
.kb img{animation:kb 16s ease-in-out infinite alternate;transform-origin:center}
@keyframes kb{from{transform:scale(1)}to{transform:scale(1.09) translate(-1.6%,1.2%)}}
.lead-cap{font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:9.5px;letter-spacing:.14em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-soft);margin-top:10px}
.stamp{position:absolute;top:20px;right:20px;width:112px;height:112px;border:2.5px solid var(--red);border-radius:50%;
  display:grid;place-content:center;text-align:center;color:var(--red);font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;
  font-size:9.5px;letter-spacing:.24em;text-transform:uppercase;line-height:1.9;transform:rotate(-12deg);z-index:3}
.stamp::before{content:"";position:absolute;inset:6px;border:1px dashed var(--red);border-radius:50%}
.js .stamp{opacity:0}
.js .in .stamp{animation:stampIn .55s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.3,1) .8s forwards}
@keyframes stampIn{from{opacity:0;transform:rotate(-12deg) scale(1.7)}to{opacity:1;transform:rotate(-12deg) scale(1)}}

/* ---------- section heads ---------- */
.sec-head{display:flex;align-items:baseline;justify-content:space-between;gap:16px;flex-wrap:wrap;
  border-bottom:2px solid var(--ink);padding-bottom:10px;margin-bottom:26px}
.sec-title{font-family:'Fraunces',Georgia,serif;font-weight:800;font-variation-settings:'WONK' 1;
  font-size:clamp(1.8rem,4.5vw,2.9rem);letter-spacing:-.01em}
.sec-title::before{content:"✦";color:var(--red);font-size:.42em;vertical-align:.4em;margin-right:.55em}
.sec-meta{font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:10px;letter-spacing:.18em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-soft)}

/* ---------- index ---------- */
.index-sec{margin-top:52px}
.index-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:4px 44px}
.idx{display:flex;align-items:baseline;text-decoration:none;font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;
  font-size:12px;letter-spacing:.04em;padding:5px 0;transition:color .2s}
.idx-no{color:var(--red);margin-right:12px}
.idx-dots{flex:1;border-bottom:2px dotted rgba(37,28,17,.35);margin:0 10px 5px;transition:border-color .2s}
.idx-pg{color:var(--ink-soft)}
.idx:hover .idx-name{text-decoration:underline;text-underline-offset:3px}
.idx:hover .idx-name,.idx:hover .idx-no{color:var(--red)}
.idx:hover .idx-dots{border-color:var(--red)}

/* ---------- ledger ---------- */
.ledger{margin-top:62px}
.ledger-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:28px;align-items:start}
.card-wrap{scroll-margin-top:90px}
.js .card-wrap{opacity:0;transform:translateY(30px);
  transition:opacity .7s ease var(--d,0ms),transform .7s cubic-bezier(.2,.65,.25,1) var(--d,0ms)}
.js .card-wrap.in{opacity:1;transform:none}
.card-wrap:nth-child(4n+1) .bill-card{--r:-.55deg}
.card-wrap:nth-child(4n+2) .bill-card{--r:.45deg}
.card-wrap:nth-child(4n+3) .bill-card{--r:-.3deg}
.card-wrap:nth-child(4n+4) .bill-card{--r:.6deg}
.bill-card{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--ink);padding:22px 24px 18px;position:relative;
  transform:rotate(var(--r,0deg));box-shadow:5px 6px 0 rgba(37,28,17,.10);scroll-margin-top:90px;
  transition:transform .4s cubic-bezier(.2,.65,.25,1),box-shadow .35s ease}
.bill-card:hover{transform:rotate(0deg) translateY(-6px);box-shadow:8px 12px 0 rgba(37,28,17,.15)}
.bill-card.flash{animation:flashRing 1.1s ease}
@keyframes flashRing{
  0%{box-shadow:5px 6px 0 rgba(37,28,17,.10),0 0 0 0 rgba(181,52,29,.55)}
  45%{box-shadow:5px 6px 0 rgba(37,28,17,.10),0 0 0 12px rgba(181,52,29,0)}
  100%{box-shadow:5px 6px 0 rgba(37,28,17,.10),0 0 0 0 rgba(181,52,29,0)}}
.card-top{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:12px;font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;
  font-size:10px;letter-spacing:.16em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-soft);margin-bottom:12px}
.card-top .no{color:var(--red);border:1px solid var(--red);padding:2px 7px}
.bill-name{font-family:'Fraunces',Georgia,serif;font-weight:720;font-variation-settings:'WONK' 1;
  font-size:1.5rem;letter-spacing:0;margin-bottom:12px;position:relative;display:inline-block}
.bill-name::after{content:"";display:block;width:44px;height:2px;background:var(--red);margin-top:6px}
.bill-card .verse{font-size:1.06rem;line-height:1.62}
.card-art{margin-top:16px}
.card-art .frame{border:1px solid var(--ink);overflow:hidden}
.card-art img{width:100%;display:block;filter:grayscale(.88) sepia(.34) contrast(1.02)}
.card-art figcaption{font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:9px;letter-spacing:.14em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-soft);padding:7px 2px 0}
.seal{position:absolute;top:14px;right:16px;width:46px;height:46px;border-radius:50%;border:2px solid var(--red);
  color:var(--red);display:grid;place-items:center;font-family:'Fraunces',serif;font-weight:800;font-size:1.35rem;
  transform:rotate(12deg) scale(1.5);opacity:0;transition:transform .35s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.3,1.2),opacity .3s}
.bill-card:hover .seal{opacity:.9;transform:rotate(-9deg) scale(1)}
/* chart (economist) */
.chart{margin-top:16px;border:1px solid var(--ink);background:var(--paper-2);padding:12px 12px 8px}
.chart svg{width:100%;height:auto;display:block}
.chart .axis{stroke:rgba(37,28,17,.5);stroke-width:1;stroke-dasharray:2 3}
.chart .line{fill:none;stroke:var(--red);stroke-width:2;stroke-dasharray:420;stroke-dashoffset:420;
  transition:stroke-dashoffset 2.6s ease .3s}
.in .chart .line{stroke-dashoffset:0}
.chart text{font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:8px;letter-spacing:.14em;fill:var(--ink-soft)}
.chart .live{fill:var(--red);animation:blink 1.6s ease-in-out infinite}
@keyframes blink{50%{opacity:.25}}
/* usage note */
.usage{grid-column:1/-1;border:2px dashed rgba(37,28,17,.5);background:var(--paper-2);padding:24px 28px;scroll-margin-top:90px}
.usage h3{font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.24em;color:var(--red);margin-bottom:12px;text-transform:uppercase}
.usage p{font-size:1.02rem;max-width:74ch;font-style:italic}
.usage .sig{font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-style:normal;font-size:10px;letter-spacing:.14em;color:var(--ink-soft);margin-top:12px;text-transform:uppercase}

/* ---------- telegram ---------- */
.telegram{margin-top:58px;background:var(--ink);color:var(--paper);border:1px solid var(--ink);
  box-shadow:10px 10px 0 var(--red);padding:34px clamp(22px,4vw,44px);position:relative;overflow:hidden;scroll-margin-top:90px}
.js .telegram{opacity:0;transform:translateY(24px);transition:opacity .8s ease,transform .8s ease}
.js .telegram.in{opacity:1;transform:none}
.tg-top{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:10px 24px;flex-wrap:wrap;
  font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:10.5px;letter-spacing:.18em;text-transform:uppercase;color:rgba(243,233,210,.7)}
.tg-big{font-family:'Fraunces',serif;font-weight:820;font-variation-settings:'WONK' 1;
  font-size:clamp(2.1rem,6vw,4.1rem);margin:20px 0 8px;letter-spacing:-.01em}
.tg-big b{color:var(--red-light);font-weight:820}
.tg-lines{font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:12.5px;letter-spacing:.04em;line-height:2.1;color:rgba(243,233,210,.85);max-width:66ch}
.tg-lines .dot{color:var(--red-light)}
.tg-sig{font-family:'Fraunces',serif;font-style:italic;font-weight:500;font-size:1.5rem;margin-top:16px}
.tg-stamp{position:absolute;right:clamp(20px,4vw,44px);bottom:28px;border:2px solid var(--red-light);color:var(--red-light);
  font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:9.5px;letter-spacing:.22em;text-transform:uppercase;text-align:center;
  padding:10px 14px;transform:rotate(6deg);line-height:1.9}
@media(max-width:640px){.tg-stamp{position:static;display:inline-block;margin-top:22px}}

/* ---------- engravings ---------- */
.engravings{margin-top:66px}
.collage{position:relative;height:600px}
.collage figure{position:absolute;width:var(--w,26%);background:#fbf3e1;border:1px solid var(--ink);
  padding:10px 10px 12px;box-shadow:7px 9px 0 rgba(37,28,17,.12);transform:rotate(var(--cr,0deg));
  transition:transform .5s cubic-bezier(.2,.65,.25,1),box-shadow .5s}
.collage figure:hover{transform:rotate(0deg) translateY(-8px);box-shadow:10px 14px 0 rgba(37,28,17,.16);z-index:5}
.collage figure::before{content:"";position:absolute;top:-11px;left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%) rotate(-2deg);
  width:76px;height:22px;background:rgba(214,178,98,.55);border:1px solid rgba(37,28,17,.15)}
.collage .frame{overflow:hidden;border:1px solid rgba(37,28,17,.35)}
.collage img{width:100%;display:block;filter:grayscale(.9) sepia(.35) contrast(1.02);transform:scale(1.02);transition:transform 6s ease}
.collage figure:hover img{transform:scale(1.13)}
.collage figcaption{font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:9px;letter-spacing:.12em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-soft);margin-top:9px}
@media(max-width:820px){
  .collage{height:auto;display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:22px}
  .collage figure{position:static;width:auto;transform:rotate(var(--cr))}
}

/* ---------- compose ---------- */
.compose{margin-top:66px;border:1px solid var(--ink);background:var(--card);
  box-shadow:9px 10px 0 rgba(37,28,17,.10);padding:32px clamp(22px,3.5vw,42px);
  display:grid;grid-template-columns:.9fr 1.1fr;gap:38px;align-items:start;scroll-margin-top:90px}
.compose .sec-title{font-size:clamp(1.6rem,3.4vw,2.3rem)}
.compose-copy{margin:14px 0 22px;font-size:1rem;max-width:40ch;font-style:italic;color:var(--ink-soft)}
.f-label{display:block;font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:10px;letter-spacing:.2em;text-transform:uppercase;margin-bottom:18px;color:var(--ink)}
.f-label input{display:block;width:100%;background:transparent;border:0;border-bottom:2px solid var(--ink);
  font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:13px;letter-spacing:.06em;color:var(--ink);padding:9px 2px;margin-top:4px}
.f-label input::placeholder{color:rgba(92,76,53,.55)}
.f-label input:focus{outline:none;border-color:var(--red)}
.compose button{margin-top:8px;cursor:pointer;background:var(--ink);color:var(--paper);border:1px solid var(--ink);
  font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.24em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:14px 26px;transition:all .25s}
.compose button:hover{background:var(--red);border-color:var(--red);transform:translate(-2px,-2px);box-shadow:4px 4px 0 var(--ink)}
.compose button:active{transform:translate(0,0);box-shadow:none}
.compose .fine{font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:9.5px;letter-spacing:.14em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-soft);margin-top:20px}
.compose-out{border:2px dashed rgba(37,28,17,.45);min-height:250px;padding:24px 22px 20px;position:relative}
.compose-out[hidden]{display:none}
.out-kicker{font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:10px;letter-spacing:.22em;color:var(--red);text-transform:uppercase;margin-bottom:14px}
.draft-stamp{position:absolute;top:14px;right:14px;border:2px solid var(--red);color:var(--red);
  font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:9px;letter-spacing:.26em;padding:6px 10px;transform:rotate(7deg);text-transform:uppercase}
.draft-stamp.pulse{animation:stampPulse .5s ease}
@keyframes stampPulse{0%{transform:rotate(7deg) scale(1.7);opacity:0}60%{transform:rotate(7deg) scale(.94);opacity:1}100%{transform:rotate(7deg) scale(1)}}
.compose-out .verse{font-size:1.15rem;line-height:1.75}
.compose-out .marg{margin-top:22px}

/* ---------- colophon ---------- */
.colophon{margin:76px 0 42px;border-top:4px solid var(--ink);position:relative;padding-top:14px}
.colophon::before{content:"";position:absolute;top:3px;left:0;right:0;border-top:1px solid var(--ink)}
.col-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1.2fr 1fr 1fr;gap:30px;padding:22px 0 26px}
.col-title{font-family:'Fraunces',serif;font-weight:820;font-variation-settings:'WONK' 1;font-size:1.7rem}
.col-title span{color:var(--red)}
.col-lines{font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:10px;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-soft);line-height:2.1}
.col-lines b{color:var(--red);font-weight:400}
.col-bottom{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:14px;flex-wrap:wrap;border-top:1px dashed rgba(37,28,17,.4);
  padding-top:14px;font-family:'Space Mono',monospace;font-size:9.5px;letter-spacing:.16em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-soft)}
.col-bottom .halb{color:var(--red)}

/* ---------- responsive ---------- */
@media(max-width:900px){
  .lead{grid-template-columns:1fr}
  .lead-text{border-right:0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--ink)}
  .ledger-grid{grid-template-columns:1fr}
  .index-grid{grid-template-columns:1fr}
  .compose{grid-template-columns:1fr}
  .mast-deck{grid-template-columns:1fr}
  .deck-lead{grid-row:auto}
  .col-grid{grid-template-columns:1fr}
}

/* ---------- reduced motion ---------- */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){
  html{scroll-behavior:auto}
  *,*::before,*::after{animation-duration:.001s!important;animation-iteration-count:1!important;transition-duration:.001s!important}
  .js .card-wrap{opacity:1;transform:none}
  .js .verse .vline>span{transform:none;transition:none}
  .js .mask-in{transform:none;animation:none}
  .js .stamp{opacity:1;animation:none}
  .js .telegram{opacity:1;transform:none}
  .ticker-track{animation:none}
  .kb img,.chart .live{animation:none}
  .in .chart .line,.chart .line{transition:none;stroke-dashoffset:0}
  .collage img{transition:none}
}
</style>
</head>
